subject: System Design
title: Monolith vs Distributed
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Monolith vs Distributed.

hook.text: A monolith puts everything in one process. A distributed system spreads work across many machines.

buildup.text: Monoliths are simple to build, test, and deploy. One codebase, one deployment, one database.

discovery.text: Distributed systems handle more load but add complexity: network failures, data sync, and debugging.

twist.text: Many successful companies ran monoliths for years. Shopify still runs one serving billions in commerce.

climax.text: Distribution is a tool, not a goal. Add complexity only when the monolith can no longer cope.

punchline.text: Start simple. Distribute when you must.

quiz.question: When should you move from a monolith to a distributed system?
options: When the monolith can no longer handle the load
From the very start of every project
